caption:
Flood season and pipeline theft are usually briefed as separate problems. They are not.

Rising water cuts ground patrol access along river-adjacent rights-of-way at the same time refining margins make tapping worth the risk. Access routes flood, foot patrols fall back, and the window for illegal connections widens — not because enforcement failed, but because the terrain did the work for the operators.

This is public knowledge across the Niger Delta and Middle Belt corridors every rainy season. A collection plan that treats flood monitoring and pipeline security as one problem, not two, is the only one that matches how the risk actually moves.

card.headline: Two risks, one calendar
card.sub: Rising water cuts ground patrol access on pipeline corridors at the same time theft economics peak. Same season, same terrain, one collection problem.

rationale: Introduces a new connective CONTEXT angle — flood season as a seasonal enabler of pipeline theft via degraded ground access — without repeating any prior dam, tap, or radar-physics framing.
